title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering during regional failover
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Production incident (SUP-4321) uncovered a race in the SLO enforcer backoff ordering when multiple region failovers happen concurrently. The existing ordering produced non-deterministic circuit-breaker signals which caused excessive load-shedding and cascading throttles. This PR contains a targeted hotfix to make regional failover ordering deterministic, tighten backoff smoothing, and add guardrails to avoid over-shedding during transient spikes. Changes: - Ensure region failover operations serialize via the failover coordinator (ordered token per customer). - Introduce a per-customer monotonic sequence for backoff updates to prevent stale overrides. - Adjust default smoothing window from 60s -> 90s to reduce oscillation. - Add a defensive check in the SLO enforcer: do not apply aggressive load-shedding unless observed error-rate > configured threshold for two consecutive evaluation cycles. - Add telemetry counters for observed ordering violations and additional tracing for failover runs. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to canary region for 2 hours with synthetic load (slo-canary job). 2) If metrics look stable, roll to remaining regions with 10% traffic ramp and monitor strongholds. 3) Post-merge follow-up: update runbooks and create a Linear ticket to review thresholds for high-throughput tenants. Backout plan: Revert the merge and re-deploy previous tag; delta is localized and the revert is expected to be fast. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for monotonic sequence and coordinator serialization added - [x] Integration test simulating concurrent regional failovers - [x] Telemetry and traces added - [x] Tested on canary and green in CI - [x] Release notes added
